entries.title: Psalms 44:1
segments:
This psalm is eminently national in its character, having been written in behalf of the suffering covenant people at a time when their enemies were triumphant over them. 
 
The history of God's dealings with his people is full of instruction, and a knowledge of it should be communicated from parents to their children.

entries.title: Psalms 44:3
segments:
The land; the land of Canaan. 
 
The mercies which men enjoy come not through their own power and goodness, but through the power and goodness of God.

entries.title: Psalms 44:5
segments: Through thy name; through thy perfections.  The name of God expresses the sum of his revealed attributes.

entries.title: Psalms 44:8
segments: Boast; acknowledge thee as our only deliverer, and glory not in our strength, but in thine alone.

entries.title: Psalms 44:9
segments: In the discipline of his people, God sometimes forsakes them "for a small moment."

Then their enemies triumph over them. But no evil can come upon them except by his permission, and for the purpose of purifying them from sin.  By this discipline he prepares his visible earthly church for greater enlargement and strength in this world, and the true spiritual members of it for glory everlasting.

entries.title: Psalms 44:10
segments: Spoil for themselves; for their own pleasure and aggrandizement.

entries.title: Psalms 44:14
segments: Byword--shaking of the head; a subject of contempt.

entries.title: Psalms 44:17
segments:
Not forgotten thee; not apostatized from God. 
 
Whatever evils may come on the true people of God, they will not forsake his service.

entries.title: Psalms 44:19
segments:
Place of dragons; desolate place where wild animals dwell.  The word here rendered "dragons" does not mean sea-monsters, which the Hebrew expresses by a different word. 
 
  Shadow of death; great and dreadful darkness.

entries.title: Psalms 44:21
segments: All things are naked and open to the all seeing eye of God, and the great concern of his people is to approve themselves to him; in their deepest troubles they feel that their help must come from him.

entries.title: Psalms 44:22
segments: Killed all the day long; continually exposed to murderous persecution.  These words, in which the ancient church expressed her bitter experience, are applied by the apostle Paul to the sufferings of Christians under the new dispensation.

entries.title: Psalms 44:23
segments: Why sleepest thou; God is represented as sleeping when he allows the enemies of his people to prevail against them.

entries.title: Psalms 44:24
segments: Forgettest our affliction; delayest to remove it.
